source_caption:
Before Tony Sirico became Paulie “Walnuts” Gualtieri in 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐨𝐩𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐨𝐬, he had already lived a life that could have inspired a gangster movie.⁣
⁣
Growing up in Brooklyn, Sirico became involved in crime at a young age. He was arrested numerous times and served prison time for offenses including robbery and weapons possession. During a prison sentence in the 1970s, he discovered acting through a performance by a group of former inmates. ⁣
⁣
After his release, Sirico decided to pursue acting, eventually appearing in films such as Goodfellas, Mighty Aphrodite and Cop Land. When he auditioned for The Sopranos, he originally wanted to play Uncle Junior. The role went to Dominic Chianese, but creator David Chase offered Sirico the part of Paulie instead. Sirico accepted on one condition: Paulie could never become a government informant. His real-life experiences helped shape the character, from his mannerisms and distinctive way of speaking to his obsession with respect and loyalty.⁣
⁣
